observations: body L1-L6: «Bouché–Leclercq» is letter-spaced; its long dash (5.3 pt) is joined to the é. The Greek ἀντιγενέσεις (L4) is set as printed. The hyphen of «sy-» (L5) prints as a raised point.

body L8-L14: the dash after «a)» measures 9.7 pt. The Greek of Tetrabiblos I, 24 is set as printed: the theta of «καϑόλου» in the open form (ϑ), and all the kappas of the passage in the curly form (ϰ); «ἀπεῤῥυηκέναι» with ῤῥ, and «ἔφ’» with an acute beside the smooth breathing (the elided ἐφ’ has none); the ι of the second «οἱ» and of «ἑπόμενοι» (L11) print broken, like a colon, and the signs over «ᾖ» (L12) print run together. «Pseudo–Proclus» and «Porphyrius» (L14) are letter-spaced; the long dash measures 5.3 pt.
body L15-L22: «‘Alī ibn Riḍwān» and «al–Battānī» are letter-spaced; the long dash of «al–Battānī» measures 5.0 pt. The dots after «altera (5):» (L19) are five.

body L23-L29: the dash after «b)» measures 9.8 pt; the dash of «11–13» is free and measures 4.3 pt, a long dash. «Ptolemaei» and «Porphyrius» are letter-spaced, and the sign of equality (L25) measures 9.7 pt. Porphyry's rays are halves before and after: 15 + 15 = 30, 12 + 12 = 24 and 9 + 9 = 18, as printed. Addenda, p. LXXIX («305–306»): al-Būnī (I, 28), after giving the sizes of the seven planets, says: «one of our sages said that the body (ǵirm) of the Sun is 15 degrees before and as many behind, the body of the Moon 12 before and as many behind, of Mars 8, of Venus 7 before and as many behind, and so also of Mercury; God the Most High knows best»; Saturn and Jupiter seem left out by the editor's carelessness, but al-Būnī plainly did not understand his source, which sets out the force of the rays in applications.
notes_left L1-L11: «Schaton», «Ptolemaei» (L4, L8, L11), «Proclum» and «Porphyrii» are letter-spaced. Note 2 ends without a full stop, as printed.

notes_right L1-L11: «Ptolemaei» and «Iulii Firmici Materni» are letter-spaced; «Pseudo-Procli» and «al-ittiṣāl» have hyphens (3.1 and 3.5 pt). «Astronomicῶn» is printed with a Greek ῶ. The signature 39 stands at the foot of the page, at the right.

notes_left L1-L2: Nallino's addenda et emendanda in Part II (p. XXVII; AB01-PDF0444-body-L013 to L015) read «adnotator ab Andrea Schatone editus» for «adnotator Schaton»: the annotator published by Andreas Schato with Paul of Alexandria's Εἰσαγωγὴ εἰς τὴν ἀποτελεσματικήν, Rudimenta in doctrinam de praedictis natalitiis (Wittenberg 1586). The printed «Adnotator Schaton» is kept.
